source_text: Ζητητέον τί βούλεται τὸ καθέζεσθαι ἐκ δεξιῶν ἢ ἐξ εὐωνύμων Ἰησοῦ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ. Συνακτέον τὰ περὶ καθέδρας Θεοῦ ἢ Χριστοῦ γεγραμμένα· ἐν Βασιλείαις εἶδεν Μιχαίας τὸν Κύριον καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου· παρὰ Ἠσαΐᾳ «εἶδον τὸν Κύριον καθήμενον ἐπὶ θρόνου ὑψηλοῦ»· ἐν Δανιὴλ «ἕως οὗ θρόνοι ἐτέθησαν, καὶ παλαιὸς ἡμερῶν ἐκάθισεν»· ἐν ψαλμῷ «Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου»· καὶ ἐν τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις «ὅταν καθίσῃ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ.» Ἴσως τὰ δεξιὰ τὰ νοητὰ καὶ ἀόρατα δημιουργήματα, τὰ δὲ ἀριστερὰ τὰ ὁρατὰ καὶ σωματικά· Χριστὸς δὲ πάντων βασιλεύει. Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: What sitting at the right and left means
orientation: Origen is explaining the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee, asking what it means to sit at Jesus' right and left in his kingdom.
pass_a_gloss: [It is] to be sought what [it] means the to sit from [the] right [side] or from [the] left [side] of Jesus in the kingdom. [It is] to be gathered together the [things] about [the] seat of God or of Christ having been written: in Kingdoms [books] Michaias saw the Lord sitting upon [a] throne; in Isaiah [it is written] "I saw the Lord sitting upon [a] throne high"; in Daniel [it is written] "until which [time] thrones were set, and [the] ancient of days sat"; in [the] psalm [it is written] "Sit from [the] right [side] of me"; and in the Gospels [it is written] "whenever sits the Son of the man upon [the] throne of glory of him." Perhaps the right [things] [are] the intelligible and invisible created [things], but the left [things] [are] the visible and bodily [things]; but Christ over all [things] reigns. Glory to Christ. Amen.

pass_b_english: We must ask what the sitting at the right or at the left of Jesus in the kingdom means. The passages written about the throne of God or of Christ must be gathered together. In Kingdoms, Micaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne. In Isaiah, “I saw the Lord sitting on a high throne” (Isaiah 6:1). In Daniel, “until thrones were set, and an Ancient of Days sat down” (Daniel 7:9). In the Psalm, “Sit at my right hand” (Psalm 110:1). And in the Gospels, “when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory” (Matthew 25:31). Perhaps the right side means the intelligible and invisible created things, and the left side the visible and bodily ones, and Christ rules over all. Glory to Christ. Amen.
